latestRelease.title: Release v2.14.5
latestRelease.notes:
## Changelog

Refer to the [2.14 Upgrade Guide](https://docs.nats.io/release-notes/whats_new/whats_new_214) for backwards compatibility notes with 2.12.x. Please note that the 2.13.x version was skipped.

### Go Version

- 1.26.5

### Dependencies

- github.com/klauspost/compress v1.19.2 (#8459)
- golang.org/x/crypto v0.55.0 (#8459)

### Added

Leafnodes

- New `dial_timeout` option can be specified in the `leafnode` config block or for specific remotes in the configuration, allowing it to be increased above the default 1 second for high-latency links (#8427)

### Fixed

General

- Fixed a deadlock that could occur in the logger when a close error occurs (#8430)

JetStream

- Fix a bug that could result in potential data loss when handling idempotent stream creates when an offline node catches up from a metalayer snapshot, caused by an incorrect update to the create time in the stream assignment (#8449)

### Complete Changes
 
https://github.com/nats-io/nats-server/compare/v2.14.4...v2.14.5

signals.title: Apply clustered expected-last-subject-sequence checks during replicated apply
signals.text: ### Proposed change Make `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence` an authoritative replicated condition for clustered streams. Today clustered publishing validates the condition before proposing the message. The condition itself is not authoritative during replicated apply: expected-subject in-flight state is leader-local, is cleared during a leader transition, and the clustered apply path deliberately skips the general consistency checks. The proposed implementation would preserve the existing pre-proposal check for fast feedback, while marking conditionally admitted replicated entries so every supporting replica rechecks the expected subject sequence against its applied stream state immediately before storage. A mismatch would deterministically reject the committed entry and advance failed-sequence accounting without storing or delivering the message. Atomic batches would reproduce the existing staged-batch restrictions and preflight all marked conditions under the stream lock before storing any batch member, preserving all-or-nothing behavior. For rolling-upgrade safety, the suggested rollout is: - all supporting binaries always understand and honor the replicated marker, regardless of their local proposal-side flag - proposal-side emission is initially behind a default-off feature flag - every possible stream peer must first run a supporting binary, then the flag must be enabled on every server that can lead the stream - effective support and enablement are verified per server through the existing startup log and `Varz.feature_flags` surface (absent = unsupported, `false` = supported but disabled, `true` = enabled) - unmarked historical entries retain their current behavior This proposal is intentionally limited to `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence`. It does not propose changing message headers, the public error model, sources/mirrors, other consistency headers, or adding a new client capability API. Before implementation I would appreciate confirmation that: 1. the replicated-marker/default-off rollout and existing operational verification surface are acceptable 2. applied per-subject store state is the intended deterministic basis for this check across supported retention modes 3. an apply-time mismatch should consume clustered failed-sequence accounting in the same way as another rejected committed stream entry 4. a marked entry with a missing or invalid predicate should fail closed as a malformed replicated command ### Use case `Nats-Expected-Last-Subject-Sequence` is used as subject-level optimistic concurrency control. A caller reads subject state at sequence S and publishes an update conditional on S still being current. For clustered streams, correctness currently depends on the leader's pre-proposal state and surrounding leadership/readiness mechanisms. The captured-term proposal fence prevents an old-term proposal, but it does not make the conditional predicate part of the replicated state-machine command. Current main has refused every transition route measured, and this proposal does not claim a reproduced production data-loss incident. The objective is to make the existing optimistic-concurrency condition authoritative at the state-machine boundary, so a committed entry whose predicate is stale cannot become valid merely because it crossed a leader transition or was replayed under different in-memory admission state. A deterministic regression can commit a current-term stale conditional entry after a newer value, proving that apply rejects it without relying on leader timing. Removing only the apply-time check then makes the stale value survive, which directly discriminates the proposed mechanism. ### Contribution Yes. I intend to contribute the implementation, including: - backward-compatible replicated encoding - default-off rollout flag and operational verification - normal, fast-batch, and atomic-batch handling - file- and memory-store tests - transform, explicit-subject, compression, restart, replay, catch-up, and sequence-accounting tests - source/mirror and feature-off compatibility tests - a deterministic apply-boundary regression and discriminating mutations
signals.author: nberlee

signals.title: (2.15) Raft proposal fast path
signals.text: Reduce contention by adding a proposal fast path that allows Propose and ProposeMulti to enqueue proposals in the hot path, without the need to acquire the raft mutex.
signals.author: sciascid

signals.title: [FIXED] Route TLS: preserve saved hostname on HostnameError when URL is an IP
signals.text: Resolves #8309. ### Problem When a route TLS connection uses a saved `tlsName` (e.g. `routeTLSName`) as the ServerName fallback — because the URL hostname is an IP (typical for gossip-discovered routes) — and the handshake fails with `x509.HostnameError`, the saved `tlsName` was cleared. This caused all subsequent reconnection attempts via gossip to use the IP as `ServerName`, which permanently fails against certificates that only have DNS SANs (no IP SANs). ### Change Add a backup field `routeTLSLastName` that stores the hostname from configured route URLs alongside `routeTLSName`. When `routeTLSName` is cleared on `HostnameError` for an IP-based route URL, restore it from the backup instead of clearing outright. The backup is consumed so that on a subsequent failure, `routeTLSName` is cleared and the IP is tried, handling both: - **DNS-only SAN certificates** (#8309): The hostname gets one retry before falling back to IP - **Mixed DNS/IP SAN environments** (#1256): After the hostname retry fails, the IP is tried on the next attempt Additionally, when a TLS handshake fails with an IP URL and `routeTLSName` is already empty but `routeTLSLastName` is available, restore `routeTLSName` from the backup for the next reconnection attempt. ### Files changed - `server/server.go`: Add `routeTLSLastName` field to `Server` struct - `server/route.go`: Save backup hostname in `saveRouteTLSName`; restore from backup on `HostnameError` for IP-based route URLs; also restore when handshake fails with empty `routeTLSName` and available backup - `server/routes_test.go`: Rewrite `TestRouteTLSNameBackupRestoreOnHostnameError` to exercise the backup restore path end-to-end, verifying `routeTLSName` is restored from `routeTLSLastName` after a simulated `HostnameError` - `server/client.go`: No changes (reverted from v1) ### Review notes - The one-extra-failure regression for IP-SAN-only peers (from the #1256 scenario) is acknowledged: the backup gives the DNS hostname one retry before falling back to IP. This adds one reconnection cycle in mixed environments but prevents permanent failure in DNS-only SAN setups. - A config reload between two `HostnameError` failures repopulates `routeTLSLastName` from `saveRouteTLSName`, restarting the one-shot backup. This is documented in the code comment. Signed-off-by: Manideep Rayala <manideep3969@gmail.com>
signals.author: Manideep3969

signals.title: (2.15) NRG: Relax SyncAlways for replicated streams
signals.text: This patch reduces the number of calls fd.Sync() for replicated streams on servers configured with `sync_interval: always`. Before this patch, the server called `fd.Sync()` for each Raft `appendEntry`, plus one `fd.Sync` on the stream's filestore for each message batched in the same `appendEntry`. This commit introduces a new internal flush policy, which syncs the stream filestore only only before creating a new snapshot. snapshot. This results in one `fd.Sync` call per raft appendEntry, plus one call for each dirty block in stream's filestore, before creating a snapshot. This leaves streams fully recoverable, while getting rid of unnecessary `fd.Sync` calls.
signals.author: sciascid
